meta.title: SiteSeer for education: construction learning in 3D
meta.description: A 3D construction site your learners walk through at any stage of the build. For construction and architecture courses, from high school to degree.

hero.statement: A 3D construction site your learners walk through at any stage of the build, from footings to fit-out. For construction and architecture courses, from high school to degree.

steps.line: Every trade, in the order they build.
Zero site risk. No PPE, no inductions.

inspect.title: Weep holes
inspect.text: A perpend left unfilled: a gap between two bricks with no mortar in it. You'll find them at the base of brick walls, and above windows like this one.

inspect.title: Lintels
inspect.text: A beam that creates the opening, carrying the brickwork above it that would otherwise be unsupported.

inspect.title: Brickwork
inspect.text: Entirely non-structural. The frame it is tied to carries the load; the brick is a protective veneer.

steps.line: Pull a layer off. See what's behind it.

pulls.title: Wall ties
pulls.text: Metal ties cross the cavity, holding the veneer to the frame against the wind.

pulls.title: Double studs
pulls.text: Used at openings in a framed wall to support the lintel, and to stiffen the opening.

steps.line: Walk in, the way you would in a game.

problem.heading: You can't take a cohort onto a building site.
problem.lede: When it's impossible to get learners onto a construction site to connect theory to practice, SiteSeer is the solution. We put a real building into a game engine, at every stage of its construction.

points.title: Nothing gets covered up.
points.text: A real site hides its own work as it goes. Here the footing, the cavity and the connection stay open.

points.title: Run it again.
points.text: Learners repeat a stage as many times as it takes, without leaving the classroom.

points.title: Learn the order of trades.
points.text: Sequencing is learned on a build instead of a slide.

problem.alt: Inside SiteSeer: a two-storey house mid-construction on a suburban site, with gum trees and site fencing
problem.caption: Inside SiteSeer: a two-storey house, part way through the build.

how.heading: Pause the build. Walk in.
how.lede: Pick a stage under the wall and watch it build. In SiteSeer it's the same idea, on a whole building.

points.title: Pick a stage.
points.text: Footings, frame, lock-up or fit-out. The building waits at that point while learners look around it.

points.title: Move through it freely.
points.text: Built in Unreal Engine, so learners walk the site in real time and go wherever they need to look.

points.title: Inspection points explain it.
points.text: Placed by people who teach construction: what you are looking at, and why it is built that way.

strip.alt: A bolted steel knee connection where a portal frame rafter meets its column
strip.caption: Steel connections, bolted as they are fabricated.

strip.alt: A timber wall frame standing on a slab beside a site workbench
strip.caption: The frame, before the lining goes on.

strip.alt: A finished raking-ceiling room with white walls, skylights and a kitchen bench
strip.caption: The same room at fit-out.

access.heading: Meet learners where they are.
access.lede: In the lab, inside your learning platform, on their own laptop or on their phone.

ways.title: Computer labs
ways.text: Deploy the Unreal Engine build to your pool and lab computers.

ways.title: Your LMS
ways.text: Embed SiteSeer in the learning platform your cohort already uses, at university, TAFE or school.

ways.title: Their laptops
ways.text: Runs on the Windows and macOS laptops learners already own. No headset, no lab booking.

ways.title: Phones and tablets
ways.text: Web versions run in the browser on iOS and Android, wherever learners are. Nothing to install.

results.heading: A decade in real classrooms.
results.lede: Over the last decade SiteSeer has been used by more than a thousand learners. Their experience shaped what it is now.

outcomes.title: Engaged learners.
outcomes.text: They come to the drawing already knowing what it describes.

outcomes.title: Relevant skills.
outcomes.text: Sequencing and trade order, learned on a build instead of a slide.

outcomes.title: Industry-ready.
outcomes.text: They have walked a build before their first day on a real one.

team.heading: Construction, education and game technology, in one team.
team.lede: SiteSeer was founded by Sean Pickersgill and Darcy Holmes, working with a research team at Adelaide University. Together they know how buildings go together, how people learn, and how to build real-time 3D worlds. That mix is rare, and it's what SiteSeer is made of.

expertise.title: Construction
expertise.text: Architecture and construction expertise: how a building is detailed, sequenced and built.
expertise.alt: Inside SiteSeer: a bolted steel knee connection where a portal frame rafter meets its column

expertise.title: Education
expertise.text: Years of teaching construction, and research into how it is learned best.
expertise.alt: Inside SiteSeer: a raking-ceiling room with sarking and insulation exposed between the framing

expertise.title: Digital technology and gamification
expertise.text: Real-time 3D in Unreal Engine, and learning designed to work the way a game does.
expertise.alt: The SiteSeer window detail coloured by building system, beside a legend of the trades that build each one

members.name: Sean Pickersgill
members.text: Founded SiteSeer to bring construction, education and game technology together, and leads the company.

members.name: Darcy Holmes
members.text: Co-founded SiteSeer and leads its technical art: the real-time Unreal Engine environments people walk through.

members.name: Associate Professor Damian Madigan
members.text: Built the first SiteSeer models and wrote the learning material they teach with, and uses SiteSeer in his own classes and lectures.

members.name: Andrew Lymn-Penning
members.text: Researches how construction is learned, and leads SiteSeer's research and development.

contact.heading: See it for yourself.
contact.lede: Book a guided demo, or talk to us about running a pilot with your cohort.

upcoming.heading: Upcoming features.
upcoming.intro: SiteSeer is continuously evolving, with a sharp focus on features that widen access and lift learning outcomes.
